next_step: Finalize spike-reliability POC design + sign NDA for security review
notes:
Summary:
- Retail CX platform for 800k monthly active customers, seasonal spikes (Nov-Dec flash sales) drive large queue backlogs.
- Current stack: homegrown routing + third-party contact center; heavy reliance on synchronous third-party NLU (cold-start failures during incidents).
- Primary ask: ensure agent assist & summarization remain available and bounded-latency during incident bursts and peak seasons. Want graceful degradation strategies.

Meeting snippets / call notes (fragments):
- 2024-10-12 FF call w/ Head of CX (Marta Alvarez): "We need responses under 150ms p95 for agent assist during peak load — anything slower causes agent frustration and extra handle time."
- SE scoping call (2024-10-30): discussed hybrid deployment (control plane in Redwood, inference in customer VPC) to satisfy data residency and compliance.
- Procurement mentioned wanting clear fallback SLAs and cost predictability; budget committee expects 12–18 month ROI case.

Technical requirements (shorthand):
- Workloads: real-time agent assist (streaming), live ticket summarization (end-of-shift batch), automated tool-calling (CRM patch actions), reranking for search.
- Targets: p95 token latency <150ms for streaming responses; sustain 200 concurrent agents generating API streams; burst capacity to 800 concurrent for 2–6 hour flash events.
- Throughput/cost: sensitive to per-token unit economics; prefer predictive reserved capacity + burst.
- Model preferences: open/quantized LLMs for on-prem inference; smaller fallback causal models for degraded mode; embeddings for rerank during heavy backpressure.
- Routing/fallback needs: region-aware routing (US east primary, EU for EU workloads), automatic fallback to low-cost model variant, and a prefix-caching layer to avoid repeated hot-start token costs.

Security/compliance notes:
- Must satisfy SOC2 + legal requires audit logging and KMS for key management.
- Data residency: customer conversations for EU customers must remain in EU VPC.
- SSO/SAML onboarding planned; security team wants a private deployment checklist before POC.

POC scope proposed:
- 3-week POC: 1) Deploy private Redwood worker pool in StormGuard VPC, 2) Validate p95 latency under synthetic peak (200 -> 800 agents), 3) Test automatic fallback behavior (model variant & embeddings-only) during induced node failures, 4) Verify audit logs to SIEM.
- Success metrics: latency thresholds met, failover within 60s, cost delta vs baseline <= 30% during peaks.

Decisioning and stakeholders:
- Champions: Marta Alvarez (Head of CX), Diego Ramos (Director of Infrastructure).
- Procurement owner: Selena Park. Security reviewer: Rajiv Menon.

Open questions (client):
- How are KV cache warmups handled on cold-starts across bursts?
- Exact sizing guidance for GPU pools to cover 800-agent bursts without excessive idle cost.
- Legal needs clarification on log retention window (currently 90 days vs Redwood default).

Next immediate actions:
- Send updated POC SOW and NDA (Ethan) — due 2024-11-08.
- SE to draft capacity-sizing options + cost comparison (Priya) — due 2024-11-12.
- Security to receive infosec questionnaire (StormGuard security) and schedule architecture deep-dive (Rajiv + Redwood security).

Notes style: brief fragments, quoted client lines, and bullets — typical CRM shorthand.
